The mlirs attached above (pp1f and pp2f) start diverging at the CloneToConsumer pass. That pass only runs on the pp2f file, and not on the pp1f file.

On the pp2f file that pass added additional duplicate tensors:

**Common to both***


**Post-CloneToConsumer for pp2f**

I don't understand why it's creating another copy of this tensor.


To test if that's the issue, I disabled the pass (CloneToConsumer) entirely. Numerical issues **persist**.

Looking at the ConvertToStream output (with the CloneTonConsumer pass disabled) I am seeing that many of the stream.X operations are missing device placement in the pp2f result but not the pp1f result. See attached MLIRs below:

[pp1f_ConvertToStream.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22644175/pp1f_ConvertToStream.mlir.txt)
[pp2f_ConvertToStream.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22644176/pp2f_ConvertToStream.mlir.txt)

This might be the same issue as https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/22081? Though I am not sure why that would be causing numerical issues.

I believe I have narrowed it down to what seems like a pretty important difference in the output of ScheduleAllocationPass:

For both cases there are 4 `_mxfp4_quant_shuffle` calls per block (8 total + 1 for definition). However, for the pp1f case the first `_mxfp4_quant_shuffle` in each block looks like this:
```mlir
  stream.cmd.dispatch @extern_dispatch::@rocm_hsaco_fb::@_mxfp4_quant_shuffle ... {
    ro %A[...] : !stream.resource<transient>{...},
    rw %A[...] : !stream.resource<transient>{...}  // Note the rw
  }
```
While for the pp2f case there are no rw calls, instead the the first `_mxfp4_quant_shuffle` call is:
```mlir
  stream.cmd.dispatch @extern_dispatch::@rocm_hsaco_fb::@_mxfp4_quant_shuffle ... {
    ro %A[...] : !stream.resource<transient>{...},
    wo %A[...] : !stream.resource<transient>{...}  // Note wo, not rw
  }
```
The other calls in the block look the same for the pp1f and pp2f mlirs:
```mlir
  stream.cmd.dispatch @extern_dispatch::@rocm_hsaco_fb::@_mxfp4_quant_shuffle ... {
    ro %B[...] : !stream.resource<transient>{...},
    wo %A[...] : !stream.resource<transient>{...}  // Note the wo
  }
```

[ScheduleAllocationPass result for pp1f](https://gist.github.com/Alex-Vasile/1dc87c564691d07d08d59c3779d58438)
[ScheduleAllocationPass result for pp2f](https://gist.github.com/Alex-Vasile/2ab33c5b6301221deeb769fb1c8442d8)


Manually patch the `wo` with `rw` does not fix the difference.

Ripping out both shuffle_scales calls from:
```MLIR
  util.func private @_asm_fp4_gemm_preshuffle_M_HALF_K_i8_N_HALF_K_i8_M_K_OVER_THIRTYTWO_i8_N_K_OVER_THIRTYTWO_i8_M_N_f32_M_N_f16(%arg0: tensor<?x?xi8>, %arg1: tensor<?x?xi8>, %arg2: tensor<?x?xi8>, %arg3: tensor<?x?xi8>, %arg4: tensor<?x?xf32>) -> tensor<?x?xf16> {
```

(and replacing `%0` and `%1` with `%arg2` and `%arg3`) produces identical results between unpipelined and pipelined!

Something with the handling of the `_mxfp4_quant_shuffle` is causing the issue.

~Going to take a closer look at the output from the `CloneToConsumer` pass which is the first place where these [two diverge](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/22124#issuecomment-3357072713).~ Can't be that pass, was still seeing numerical issues when I had disabled it entirely.

[PP1](https://gist.github.com/Alex-Vasile/9a8dcfa71d2b83d92e6b50a16afef09e)
[PP2](https://gist.github.com/Alex-Vasile/3bb3e549adbf1cfea659cc1fb9b2c0df)

I think I have a (even more) minimal reproducer for the issue. It looks like buffer offsets are not getting calculated correctly when we have a RW buffer that passed between devices.

Ok that last one may have been a red herring, it looked like it was calculating the offset wrong (
```mlir
builtin.module {
      func.func @test_dispatch_0_matmul_4x8x8_f32(%arg0: !stream.binding {stream.alignment = 64 : index}, %arg1: !stream.binding {stream.alignment = 64 : index}, %arg2: !stream.binding {stream.alignment = 64 : index}) {

        %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
        %c256 = arith.constant 256 : index

        %1 = stream.binding.subspan %arg1[%c0] : !stream.binding -> !iree_tensor_ext.dispatch.tensor<readonly:tensor<8x8xf32>>
        %2 = stream.binding.subspan %arg2[%c256] : !stream.binding -> !iree_tensor_ext.dispatch.tensor<readwrite:tensor<4x16xf32>>
```

(where the `%c256 was %0 in the single-device model).

However then we copy the value from %c256 -> to the 0th place in the buffer here:
```mlir
      stream.cmd.copy %arg6[%c256], %arg5[%c0], %c256 : !stream.resource<transient>{%c512} -> !stream.resource<external>{%c256}
      stream.cmd.flush to(#hal.device.affinity<@__device_1>) %arg5[%c0 for %c256] : !stream.resource<external>{%c256}
```

The issue may be be in `FoldUniformOperandsPass` 

It is somehow replacing the operands in
```stream.cmd.dispatch @decode_bs4$async_dispatch_3::@decode_bs4$async_dispatch_3_slow_memcpy[%c256, %c1024](%c1740800_i32, %c0_i32, %c0_i32, %c0_i32, %c256_i32, %c0_i32, %c1024_i32, %c0_i32 : i32, i32, i32, i32, i32, i32, i32, i32) {```

with a zero-offset

Compiling [kv1.mlir](https://gist.github.com/Alex-Vasile/9a8dcfa71d2b83d92e6b50a16afef09e) and [kv2.mlir](https://gist.github.com/Alex-Vasile/3bb3e549adbf1cfea659cc1fb9b2c0df) to stream I then manually edited the files. Instead of disable both calls to `shuffle_scales` inside `_asm_fp4_gemm_...`, I first disabled them one at a time:
```mlir
    %0 = util.call @shuffle_scales(%arg2) : (tensor<?x?xi8>) -> tensor<?x?xi8>
    %1 = util.call @shuffle_scales(%arg3) : (tensor<?x?xi8>) -> tensor<?x?xi8>
    %2 = util.call @asm_mxfp4_gemm(%arg0, %arg1, %0, %1, %arg4) : (tensor<?x?xi8>, tensor<?x?xi8>, tensor<?x?xi8>, tensor<?x?xi8>, tensor<?x?xf32>) -> tensor<?x?xf16>
    util.return %2 : tensor<?x?xf16>
```

Replacing `%0` with `%arg2` no longer produces numerical differences. But, instead if I replace `%1` with `%arg3` (and use `%0`) I **get** numerical differences.

The attached [mlir files](https://gist.github.com/Alex-Vasile/1a26726bc6da8c9c87c397abf03362e0) has `_asm_fp4_gemm_...` replaced with two variants, `PASSES` where `%0` is replaced and `FAILS` where `%1` is replaced.

There are 4 calls to `_asm_fp4_gemm_...` (2 on each device), going through all 16 combinations it turns out that some of the `PASSES` calls can be replaced with `FAILS`. Numerical differences occur only if both calls to `PASSES` for a device are replaced with `FAILS`. Replacing only 1 (including the case where 1 call is replaced on both devices) does **not** produces numerical differences between unpipelined and pipelined.

I put together a small intepreter that reads the entire stream.mlir files generated, and tracks all of the memory accesses (reads and writes), it propagates the reads/writes through operations and tags them with their ancestry. 
https://gist.github.com/AWoloszyn/579db4fa0ec1ff26ae53d8b5c6064d34

The results for both of the stream.mlir files are the same (at least barring any bugs in my implementation). The final output matches (modulo some SSA values) meaning I don't think we have a memory offset issue.

issue.body:
### What happened?

I am seeing numerical differences between a trimmed down model when operating across 2 devices. I've tracked it down to the interaction of the following ops:
```python
	q = self.attn_q(x)
	k = self.attn_k(x)
	v = self.attn_v(x)
```
Which will performs a matmul on each using an asembly kernel.

Having all three matmuls performed produces numerical differences in the final result between pipeline parallelism of 2 and an unpipelined model. 

If **any** 1 of the `self.attn_q` calls is replaced with one of the following
```python
	q = x[..., : self.head_count * self.head_dim]
	k = x[..., : self.head_count_kv * self.head_dim]
	v = x[..., : self.head_count_kv * self.head_dim]
```
The results remain different between PP2 and unpipelined.

If however **any** 2 of the 3 are replaced, then the results become identical

I'm attaching all 7 permutations of the input mlirs. `_pp` indicates the pipelined version `_qkv` indicates that all three `q`, `k`, `v` values are calculated using the `self.attn_` calls; `_qk` indicates that only `q` and `k` are calculated using them, etc.
**Passing**
- [model_q.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22567341/model_q.mlir.txt)
- [model_k.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22567346/model_k.mlir.txt)
- [model_v.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22567344/model_v.mlir.txt)

- [model_pp_v.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22567343/model_pp_v.mlir.txt)

**Failing**
- [model_qkv.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22567355/model_qkv.mlir.txt)
- [model_qk.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22567359/model_qk.mlir.txt)
- [model_qv.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22567360/model_qv.mlir.txt)

- [model_pp_qkv.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22567358/model_pp_qkv.mlir.txt)
- [model_pp_qk.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22567354/model_pp_qk.mlir.txt)
- [model_pp_qv.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22567357/model_pp_qv.mlir.txt)
- [model_pp_kv.mlir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22567356/model_pp_kv.mlir.txt)

### Steps to reproduce your issue

**Compile command**
```
iree-compile $MLIR_PATH \
    -o=$VMFB_PATH \
    --iree-hal-target-device="hip[0]" \
    --iree-hal-target-device="hip[1]" \
    --iree-hal-target-device="hip[2]" \
    --iree-hal-target-device="hip[3]" \
    --iree-hal-target-device="hip[4]" \
    --iree-hal-target-device="hip[5]" \
    --iree-hal-target-device="hip[6]" \
    --iree-hal-target-device="hip[7]" \
    --iree-hip-target=gfx950 \
    --iree-opt-level=O3 \
    --iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-collapse-across-expands=true \
    --iree-codegen-enable-default-tuning-specs=true \
    --iree-hip-enable-tensor-ukernels \
    --iree-hal-indirect-command-buffers=true \
    --iree-stream-resource-memory-model=discrete \
    --iree-hip-specialize-dispatches \
    --iree-hal-memoization=true \
	--iree-opt-const-expr-hoisting=false \
    --iree-stream-affinity-solver-max-iterations=1024
```

**Run command**
Pipelined version
```
	ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 iree-run-module  \
		--hip_use_streams=true \
		--module=$VMFB_PATH \
		--parameters=model=$IRPA_PATH \
		--device=hip://0 --device=hip://1 --device=hip://2 --device=hip://3 \
		--device=hip://4 --device=hip://5 --device=hip://6 --device=hip://7 \
		--input=4x1xi64=2 \
		--input=4xi64=1 \
		--input=4xi64=0 \
		--input=4x1xi64 \
		--input=3x4128768xf8E4M3FN \
		--input=3x4128768xf8E4M3FN \
		--output=@"result0${OVERRIDE_NAME}.npy" \
		--function=decode_bs4
```

Unpipelined version
```
	ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 iree-run-module  \
		--hip_use_streams=true \
		--module=$VMFB_PATH \
		--parameters=model=$IRPA_PATH \
		--device=hip://0 --device=hip://1 --device=hip://2 --device=hip://3 \
		--device=hip://4 --device=hip://5 --device=hip://6 --device=hip://7 \
		--input=4x1xi64=2 \
		--input=4xi64=1 \
		--input=4xi64=0 \
		--input=4x1xi64 \
		--input=3x8257536xf8E4M3FN \
		--output=@"result0${OVERRIDE_NAME}.npy" \
		--function=decode_bs4
```

### What component(s) does this issue relate to?

Compiler

### Version information

`iree-3.8.0rc20250923`

### Additional context

_No response_

issue.body:
Hi, IREE developers. I'm tring to use `iree-compile` and `iree-run-module` to deploy a simple collective reduce-add case written in StableHlO MLIR : ```mlir func.func @main(%input : tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xf32> { %out = "stablehlo.all_reduce"(%input) ({ ^bb0(%arg0: tensor, %arg1: tensor): %sum = stablehlo.add %arg0, %arg1 : tensor stablehlo.return %sum : tensor }) {channel_handle = #stablehlo.channel_handle, replica_groups = dense<[[0, 1]]> : tensor<1x2xi64>, use_global_device_ids} : (tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xf32> return %out : tensor<4xf32> } ``` I have two CUDA cards on my machine, and I want to use these two cards to perform a simple reduce-add task. I compile the mlir file by using the following command: ```sh iree-compile - --iree-hal-target-device=cuda[0] --iree-hal-target-device=cuda[1] -mlir-print-ir-after-all --iree-hal-dump-executable-intermediates-to=./ ./allReduce.mlir -o ./output.vmfb > dump.mlir 2>&1 ``` then I tried the following command to run this output module: ```sh CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 iree-run-module --module=./output.vmfb --function=main --input="4xf32=[1,2,3,4]" --device=cuda://0 --device=cuda://1 ``` but I got the following exception: 
iree/runtime/src/iree/hal/drivers/cuda/cuda_device.c:798: INVALID_ARGUMENT; 
default collective channel ID requested but no channel provider has been set on the device to provide it; 
while invoking native function hal.channel.create; while calling import;
it seems like we don't have channal provider for cuda platform? I've seen a similar issue before: https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/21503 While tracing the source code, I found that currently only channel provider will be created for MPI by default? https://github.com/iree-org/iree/blob/39c572deb0d388eb86d78295896a6e38835ccc8c/runtime/src/iree/tooling/device_util.c#L310-L326 But I found that the hip platform seems to be callable for mlir input by using the analogous command: https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/22124 So, my question is, how can I run this reduce-add mlir example on a CUDA platform using iree-run-module/iree-run-mlir? Or does it mean that the CUDA platform currently only supports running MLIR with collective operations in IREE through interfaces like MPI? Or Is it just because I haven't set the MPI/NCCL environment variables on my platform that this case can't be run? Any help would be grateful, thanks!
